title: Kissing-number lower bounds
summary: The kissing-number problem asks how many nonoverlapping unit spheres can touch a central unit sphere. New configurations improve 15 long-standing lower bounds for kissing numbers and related spherical codes.

title: Erdős problem survey
summary: A survey of 700 problems marked open in the Erdős database found five apparently new solutions and eight problems whose earlier solutions had been overlooked.

title: Erdős unit-distance conjecture
ai: OpenAI frontier model (specific version not disclosed) + Noga Alon + Thomas Bloom + Timothy Gowers + Daniel Litt + Will Sawin + Jacob Tsimerman + Melanie Matchett Wood
summary: The unit-distance problem asks how many pairs among a given number of planar points can be exactly one unit apart. The conjectured asymptotic upper bound is disproved by a denser infinite family of configurations.

title: Erdős and OEIS conjecture proofs
summary: A formal proof-search study resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems and proved 44 of 492 conjectures selected from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences.

title: Cycle double cover conjecture
summary: The cycle double cover conjecture states that every bridgeless graph has a collection of cycles covering each edge exactly twice. The reported proof establishes this long-standing graph-theory statement.

title: Jacobian conjecture
summary: The Jacobian conjecture states that every complex polynomial map with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant has a polynomial inverse. A three-variable counterexample disproves the conjecture in dimensions three and above; the plane case remains open.

title: Dinitz–Garg–Goemans conjecture
summary: The conjecture proposed a cost-preserving way to round divisible multicommodity flows into unsplittable flows under a capacity margin. A network whose best divisible and unsplittable costs differ provides a counterexample.

title: Crouzeix’s conjecture
summary: Crouzeix’s conjecture states that evaluating a polynomial on a complex matrix increases its norm by at most twice its maximum over the numerical range. The sharp constant 2 is established.

title: Ten mathematical advances
summary: A single research release presented ten results across mathematics and theoretical computer science, including advances on sofic groups, operator-algebra rigidity, and high-dimensional sphere packing.

title: Sendov’s conjecture
summary: Sendov’s conjecture states that every zero of a polynomial whose zeros lie in the unit disk is within distance one of a critical point. The result settles the statement for every polynomial degree.

title: Riemann zeta zeros on the critical line
ai: Claude (unreleased research version) + Jarred Sumner + Levent Alpöge + Ralph Furman + Eric Easley
summary: The Riemann hypothesis places every nontrivial zeta zero on the critical line. This unconditional result raises the known proportion of simple zeros on that line to at least 67.25 percent; it does not prove the hypothesis.

title: Hadamard matrices below order 2000
summary: The Hadamard conjecture predicts a plus-or-minus-one matrix of every positive order divisible by four with mutually orthogonal rows. Explicit matrices settle the twelve previously unresolved admissible orders below 2000; the general conjecture remains open.

title: OEIS conjecture campaign
summary: A large-scale study of open conjectures from the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences reported 147 proofs or counterexamples, measuring how automated conjecture solving scales across a broad corpus.

title: Elliptic-curve rank 31
summary: Whether elliptic curves over the rationals have unbounded rank remains open. An explicit curve with 31 independent rational points raises the unconditional record to at least 31; exact rank claims require additional conjectural assumptions.

title: Complex structure on the six-sphere
summary: Hopf’s 1948 problem asks whether the six-sphere admits an integrable complex structure. The manuscript claims an explicit complex threefold diffeomorphic to the six-sphere; the result awaits independent verification.

title: Large prime-gap lower bound
ai: GPT 5.6 Sol + DottedCalculator (prompting and submission) + Boris Alexeev (Lean formalisation)
summary: The large-gap problem asks how far apart consecutive primes can be infinitely often. A tilted residue-class construction improves the preceding asymptotic lower bound by an unbounded iterated-logarithm factor.

title: Bounded prime gaps at 186
summary: The bounded-gaps problem asks how close together consecutive primes can occur infinitely often. Subject to three stated analytic and numerical inputs, this result lowers the unconditional upper bound to 186; the twin-prime target remains 2.

title: Critical bond percolation in every dimension
ai: Anthropic Claude models (specific version undisclosed) + Justin Leder
summary: For nearest-neighbor bond percolation on the integer lattice, the question asks whether an infinite open cluster exists at the critical probability. The reported result proves that the probability of such a cluster at criticality is zero in every dimension at least two.

title: Kozma–Nitzan percolation conjectures
summary: The remaining Kozma–Nitzan conjectures concern critical behavior in percolation. A follow-up project reports proofs and formalizations extending the result on the absence of critical infinite clusters.

title: Fermat’s Last Theorem formalization
summary: Fermat’s Last Theorem states that no three positive integers satisfy aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for n greater than two. Its classical proof has been translated into a computer-checkable formal development.

title: Köthe’s conjecture
summary: Köthe’s conjecture asks whether the sum of two nil left ideals is always nil. A constructed ring contains a nil ideal whose two-by-two matrix ideal has a nonnilpotent element, disproving the conjecture.

title: Navier–Stokes breakdown with smooth forcing
summary: The Clay problem asks whether smooth three-dimensional Navier–Stokes data can develop a finite-time singularity. The reported solution uses smooth external forcing, addressing the permitted forced formulations while leaving the unforced case unresolved.

title: Ibragimov–Iosifescu central limit conjecture
summary: The conjecture predicted a central limit theorem for stationary, φ-mixing sequences with finite variance and diverging partial-sum variance. A counterexample shows that normalized sums can instead converge to zero along a subsequence.

title: Boussinesq blowup with smooth forcing
ai: Claude, Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol + Levent Alpöge + Tristan Buckmaster
summary: The inviscid Boussinesq problem asks whether smooth initial data and space-time smooth forcing can produce a finite-time singularity. The reported construction gives such blowup on the plane while the temperature remains bounded.

title: Euler blowup with smooth forcing
ai: Claude, Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol + Levent Alpöge + Tristan Buckmaster
summary: The three-dimensional incompressible Euler problem asks whether a smooth flow can lose regularity in finite time. The reported construction produces genuine blowup from smooth data under space-time smooth forcing.

title: Bounded prime gaps at 212
ai: AxiomProver + François Charton + Letong Hong + Kenny Lau + Ken Ono + Guillaume Remy + Ho Chung Siu + Ashvin A. Swaminathan + Jesse Thorner + Yunzhou Xie
summary: The bounded-gaps problem asks how close together consecutive primes can occur infinitely often. This result proved that infinitely many consecutive prime pairs differ by at most 212, improving the previous bound of 240.

title: Smale’s mean value conjecture
summary: Smale asked whether the universal constant in his mean value theorem for complex polynomials could be reduced from 4 to 1. A polynomial counterexample shows that the constant 1 is impossible.

title: Maximal prime-gap lower bound
summary: The maximal prime-gap problem asks how large gaps between consecutive primes can become. This result improves the asymptotic lower bound through a stronger short-translates theorem combined with an Erdős–Rankin covering argument.

title: Bounded prime gaps at 236
summary: The bounded-gaps problem asks how close together consecutive primes can occur infinitely often. This announcement established an upper bound of 236, improving 240 before being superseded by stronger results.

title: Four-uniform Erdős matching conjecture
ai: GPT-5.6 Sol; Astra; GPT-5 Pro; GPT-6 Pro
summary: The Erdős matching conjecture gives the maximum size of a uniform set family with bounded matching number. The reported result settles every parameter in the four-uniform case; higher uniformities remain open.

title: Erdős problem 1: sum-distinct sets
summary: A set is sum-distinct when all of its subset sums differ. Erdős proposed a universal exponential lower bound on the containing interval; arbitrarily large counterexamples show that no such constant-factor bound exists.

title: Erdős problem 571: bipartite Turán exponents
summary: This problem asks which growth exponents occur as Turán numbers of a single bipartite graph. The result realizes every rational exponent from 1 up to, but not including, 2.

title: Erdős problem 548: Erdős–Sós conjecture
summary: The Erdős–Sós conjecture states that a graph with average degree greater than k − 1 contains every tree with k edges. The reported result establishes the full density statement.

title: Nevanlinna’s half-plane problem
ai: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra + Quanyu Tang + Bokai Cui + Wei He + Tao Hu + Yanyang Li + Ke Wang + Zijun Yu
summary: Nevanlinna asked whether a meromorphic function omitting three values in a half-plane must be of bounded type there. A real meromorphic counterexample gives a negative answer for both half-planes.

title: de Bruijn–Newman constant upper bound
ai: Claude; ChatGPT and Codex (versions undisclosed) + Jude Gomila
summary: The de Bruijn–Newman constant measures when zeros in a heat-flow deformation of the Riemann xi function become entirely real. Its upper bound is reduced to 0.1787854; the Riemann hypothesis corresponds to a bound of zero.

title: Elliptic-curve rank 30
summary: Whether elliptic curves over the rationals have unbounded rank remains open. An explicit curve with 30 independent rational points raised the unconditional record before a rank-31 example superseded it three days later.

title: Marton’s inner-bound conjecture
ai: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5 + Mian Huang + Yanxiao Liu + Yi Liu
summary: Marton’s inner bound is the best-known achievable rate region for a general broadcast channel. A finite two-receiver channel shows that its one-letter form does not always equal the full capacity region.

title: Smooth Carathéodory conjecture
ai: Claude, Codex + Levent Alpöge + John-Paul Smith
summary: Carathéodory asked whether every closed convex surface in three-dimensional space has at least two umbilic points. A smooth convex sphere with exactly one umbilic disproves the smooth case; the real-analytic theorem remains valid.

title: Matrix-multiplication exponent
ai: AlphaEvolve + Emilien Dupont + Marvin Eisenberger + Borislav Kozlovskii + Abbas Mehrabian + Francisco J. R. Ruiz + Abigail See + Renfei Zhou + Josh Alman + Virginia Vassilevska Williams + Matej Balog
summary: The matrix-multiplication exponent measures the asymptotic cost of multiplying square matrices. Its upper bound is lowered from 2.371339 to 2.371177, while the central question of whether the exponent equals 2 remains open.

title: Banach’s isometric conjecture
ai: ChatGPT 5.6 Pro, ChatGPT 5.5 Pro + Xinbao Lu + Kaiwen Yang
summary: Banach asked whether a real normed space must be a Hilbert space when all subspaces of a fixed intermediate dimension are mutually isometric. Resolving the remaining odd-dimensional cases completes the conjecture over the reals.

title: Schiffer’s conjecture
ai: GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Fable 5 + Gonzalo Cao-Labora + Jaume de Dios Pont
summary: Schiffer’s conjecture asks whether a bounded domain admitting a Neumann eigenfunction constant on its boundary must be a ball. Infinitely many noncircular planar domains provide counterexamples and also resolve the equivalent Pompeiu problem negatively.

title: Existence of non-sofic groups
summary: Gromov and Weiss asked whether every group admits approximate finite permutation representations, making every group sofic. An explicit construction answers no by producing a non-sofic group.

title: Connes’ rigidity conjecture
summary: Connes’ rigidity conjecture asks whether ICC property-(T) groups are determined by their group von Neumann algebras. A counterexample shows that nonisomorphic groups can have isomorphic associated algebras.

title: High-dimensional sphere-packing bounds
summary: The sphere-packing problem asks how densely equal spheres can fill high-dimensional space. The asymptotic upper bound is improved beyond the long-standing Kabatiansky–Levenshtein bound to the Cohn–Elkies linear-programming threshold.

title: KLS conjecture for quadratic forms
summary: The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture seeks dimension-free variance bounds for isotropic log-concave distributions. The quadratic-form case is established with constant 2, alongside an improved general bound.

title: Petersen coloring conjecture
summary: Jaeger conjectured that every bridgeless cubic graph admits a Petersen coloring. An explicit bridgeless cubic counterexample disproves the conjecture, while its consequences such as Berge–Fulkerson remain open.

title: White’s matroid conjecture
ai: ChatGPT-5.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8 + Matt Larson
summary: White conjectured that symmetric exchange binomials generate every matroid toric ideal. A rank-nine binary matroid supplies a counterexample.

title: Real sum-product conjecture
ai: GPT-5.5 Pro + Thomas F. Bloom + Will Sawin + Carl Schildkraut + Dmitrii Zakharov
summary: The real sum-product conjecture predicted that every finite real set has nearly quadratically many sums or products. Families of algebraic integers with substantially fewer of both provide counterexamples.
